chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hanaan, from Abu Kahma, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the juice (of grapes), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I have a vineyard and I press it every year, and I put it in jugs, and I sell it before it boils.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it. But if it boils, then its sale is not permissible.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is so; we sell our dates to those we know make wine from them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling grape juice before and after it ferments into wine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *tabdil* (transformation) in intoxicants, ruling that grape juice (*asir*) is permissible to sell as long as it has not fermented into wine (*khamr*). He reinforces this by noting that the Ahl al-Bayt themselves sold dates to those known to produce wine, demonstrating that the sale of the raw material remains valid even if the buyer uses it for intoxication, provided the transformation has not yet occurred.
